target_customer: Nigerian FMCG distributors and SME to mid-market finance teams that pay and collect from other businesses
problem: B2B payments in Nigeria involve slow settlement, manual invoicing and reconciliation; a survey cited by TechCrunch found many businesses wait over 24 hours for payments.
business_model: Payments and spend management platform earning fees on payment flows plus software and B2B credit products
product_category: B2B payments and financial operating system

founders.name: Yele Oyekola
prior_employers: United Nations in Africa (economic policy officer)

founders.name: Tunde Akinnuwa
education: HEC Paris MBA (per Poets and Quants, filed under HEC Paris)

founders.name: Emeka Okwuagwu
founders.background_notes: Named by TechCrunch; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payment collection and disbursement, invoicing and ERP integrations (SAP, Dynamics, QuickBooks, Sage per TechCrunch) in Nigeria; a CBN license was later needed.

defensibility.rationale: Embedding in distributor workflows and ERP integrations creates switching costs; the company later cites a CBN PSSP license, ISO 27001 and PCI DSS.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Poets and Quants quotes the founder saying large FMCG firms work with banks on payment tools that he considers insufficient; no bank copy or acquisition found.

market_need_then: TechCrunch cites a 1.5 trillion USD sub-Saharan B2B payments market and a survey of 1,000 business owners where 44 percent waited over 24 hours for payments.

identity.voice_and_tone: Trust and compliance led: local-first, licensed, certified

branding.brand_signature: Venmo for B2B in Africa positioning line

brand_strength.rationale: Name shared with the LEGO Duplo line and Duplo International, which hurts search; the brand is mostly a pitch line and compliance badges.

outcome_analysis: Duplo launched in 2021 with FMCG distributors, raised 1.3M USD pre-seed in February 2022 and 4.3M USD seed in August 2022 for 5.6M total, and reported very fast payment volume growth. It is active and has expanded to treasury and e-invoicing with a South African arm. No later priced round was found in searches, so funding coverage is partial and the long run outcome is open.
notes: Competitors: the YC page, company site, both TechCrunch articles and Poets and Quants named none, and two searches gave no dated rival, so the list is empty rather than known to be empty. Seed investor list taken from a search summary of People of Color in Tech and Techloy, with TechCrunch as the cited source. Founders' education beyond the HEC Paris MBA not found. Searches for later news returned results about unrelated companies, so no layoff or exit information was found.
